responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Adapteva Epiphany architecture, covering the machine-specific logic that turns generic RTL and target hooks into Epiphany ISA, ABI, and operating-environment behavior. Its core files define the architectural configuration and command-line options, implement calling convention, register usage, addressing, prologue/epilogue expansion, asm output, costing, attributes, and other target hooks, and describe the actual instruction set through RTL patterns, operand predicates, constraints, machine modes, and DFA scheduling data. A distinctive responsibility of this port is its handling of Epiphany floating-point and mode-switch state, including dedicated support passes that expose and resolve software FP mode transitions so later RTL stages can schedule and emit correct code. The module also includes user-facing intrinsic declarations and OS overlay support such as RTEMS integration, making it the complete code-generation subsystem that distinguishes Epiphany-specific instruction selection, scheduling, ABI rules, and low-level emission from neighboring GCC target directories.
